guitar.notes: Paul Gilbert's long-running signature relationship with Ibanez (PGM series) is well documented in the shred-guitar community.

tone.target: bright hard-rock crunch with wah bite and clean-picked clarity
tone.profile: bright hard-rock crunch with wah bite and clean-picked clarity
tone.summary: A tight signal chain featuring a Boost/OD pre-amp for clarity, followed by a Wah pedal, leading into a Marshall-style amp model (UK 45) paired with a bright 4x12 cabinet to achieve bright hard-rock crunch and arpeggiated clarity.
corrections: Use wah as the signature effect

rig.name: Mr. Big - Daddy, Brother, Lover, Little Boy - Valeton GP-180

blocks.purpose: Clean up hum and background noise.
Provide tight midrange crunch and boost clarity for arpeggios.
blocks.gap: The Blues OD is chosen over Green OD/OD 9 to provide a slightly more open, classic rock voicing suitable for the Plexi style.

blocks.purpose: Implement the signature wah sweep effect.
Used as a secondary gain stage if more bite is needed, but kept off to maintain clarity.
blocks.gap: The primary crunch comes from the Blues OD and Amp model; this slot acts as an optional boost/grit layer.

blocks.purpose: Simulate the Marshall/Plexi style amp for classic hard-rock tone and brightness.
Provide the classic 4x12 cabinet voicing required for hard rock.
Enhance the midrange crunch and bright top end while controlling excessive low-end mud.
Optional subtle thickening for arpeggios; kept off to avoid sounding too '80s' or muddy.
blocks.gap: The verdict explicitly avoids chorus, so this is a minimal/optional slot. It could be replaced by Tremolo if needed.

blocks.purpose: Add subtle rhythmic depth to the arpeggios without washing out the crunch.
Provide a natural sense of space without heavy reverb.

improvements.summary: Improve cabinet realism and overall brightness to match the bright hard-rock crunch required.

proposals.reason: Enhance top end and punch for modern hard rock clarity.
